subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Early stage and locally advanced NSCLC: staging, neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, surgical resection and adjuvant targeted therapy

steps.tx: Anatomical **lobectomy** accompanied by systematic hilar and mediastinal lymph node dissection represents the established surgical standard of care for medically operable clinical stage I and II non-small cell lung cancer. Complete resection requires harvesting at least three mediastinal nodal stations, including subcarinal node station 7. Complete nodal sampling provides rigorous pathological staging that dictates whether subsequent adjuvant systemic therapy is required.

steps.tx: In completely resected stage IB to IIIA EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, the landmark **ADAURA trial** established **adjuvant osimertinib** for 3 years as standard therapy. Third-generation EGFR inhibition demonstrated a remarkable disease-free survival benefit and significantly prolonged overall survival compared to placebo. Adjuvant osimertinib profoundly suppressed distant metastatic recurrence, particularly reducing central nervous system relapse by over 80%.

steps.tx: The pivotal **CheckMate 816** trial revolutionized the neoadjuvant landscape by combining **neoadjuvant nivolumab** with platinum doublet chemotherapy for 3 cycles prior to surgical resection in resectable stage IB to IIIA NSCLC. This combination produced a dramatic rise in pathological complete response rates from 2% with chemotherapy alone to 24%, translating into statistically significant improvements in event-free survival without compromising surgical resection rates or safety.

points: Nivolumab plus platinum doublet x 3 cycles
Does not compromise curative surgical resection

right.title: Chemotherapy Alone
points: Higher rate of early metastatic relapse

steps.tx: Broadening the perioperative approach, the **KEYNOTE-671** phase III trial evaluated **perioperative pembrolizumab** administered alongside neoadjuvant cisplatin doublet chemotherapy for 4 cycles, followed by surgical resection and adjuvant pembrolizumab for up to 1 year. The trial demonstrated statistically significant improvements in both event-free survival and definitive overall survival in resectable stage II to IIIB non-small cell lung cancer.

steps.tx: In unresectable locally advanced stage III NSCLC without disease progression after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy, the landmark **PACIFIC trial** established **consolidation durvalumab** as the global standard of care. Administered every 2 weeks for up to 12 months, durvalumab immune checkpoint blockade significantly improved progression-free survival and achieved a durable overall survival benefit, raising 5-year survival rates to approximately 43%.

left.title: PACIFIC Durvalumab Arm
points: Standard of care following concurrent CRT

right.title: Placebo Arm (Historical)
points: Higher rate of systemic distant metastases

steps.tx: For unresectable stage III disease, **concurrent chemoradiation** is the standard approach, with radiotherapy delivered alongside platinum-based chemotherapy. In patients who have not progressed after chemoradiation, **consolidative anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy** for up to one year improved progression-free and overall survival in the PACIFIC trial. For medically inoperable stage I tumours, **stereotactic body radiotherapy** (SBRT) is the preferred ablative option, giving high local control in peripheral lesions.

steps.tx: In completely resected stage IB to IIIA ALK-rearranged NSCLC, the phase III **ALINA** trial established **adjuvant alectinib** for up to 2 years as a superior alternative to platinum-based chemotherapy. Alectinib reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by an unprecedented 76%, while demonstrating profound protection against central nervous system recurrence, firmly establishing targeted TKI therapy in early-stage ALK-positive disease.

steps.tx: Targeted **Stereotactic body radiotherapy** delivers excellent **local control** exceeding 90% in medically inoperable stage I peripheral non-small cell lung cancer. Delivering biological effective doses exceeding 100 Gy across 3 to 5 fractions achieves definitive tumour ablation without requiring open surgical resection. Radiotherapy provides an outstanding curative option for patients with severe cardiopulmonary comorbidities.

steps.tx: Definitive **concurrent chemoradiation** combining 60 to 66 Gy of thoracic radiation with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy represents the foundation of therapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC. Standard regimens incorporate cisplatin paired with either etoposide or pemetrexed for non-squamous histology. Concurrent administration provides superior overall survival compared with sequential treatment by maximizing radiosensitisation and controlling micrometastatic systemic disease.
